verses.t: Mencius said, "Even with the keen sight of Li Lou and the skill of Gongshu [Ban], without compass and square you cannot make circles and squares. Even with the sharp hearing of Music-master Kuang, without the six pitch-pipes you cannot set the five notes right. Even with the Way of Yao and Shun, without benevolent government you cannot bring the world to peace and order. There are rulers today who have benevolent hearts and a reputation for benevolence, yet the people do not receive their bounty and they cannot be models for later ages, because they do not practise the Way of the former kings. Therefore it is said, 'Goodness alone is not enough for governing; laws alone cannot carry themselves out.' The Ode says, 'Without error, without forgetting, following the old statutes.' No one has ever gone wrong by following the laws of the former kings. When the sages had used their eyes to the utmost, they added the compass and square, the level and the plumb-line, for making things square, round, level and straight, and these have been of endless use. When they had used their ears to the utmost, they added the six pitch-pipes for setting the five notes right, and these have been of endless use. When they had used their minds to the utmost, they added a government that could not bear to see people suffer, and their benevolence covered the world. Therefore it is said, 'To build high, you must start from hills and mounds; to dig low, you must start from rivers and marshes.' Can one who governs without following the Way of the former kings be called wise? This is why only the benevolent should be in high places. When one who is not benevolent is in a high place, he spreads his wickedness among the multitude. When those above have no principles to measure by, and those below have no laws to keep; when the court does not trust in the Way and the workmen do not trust in measures; when gentlemen offend against righteousness and small men offend against the law, then it is only by luck that the state survives. Therefore it is said, 'Inner and outer walls that are not complete, and weapons and armour that are few, are not the calamity of a state. Fields not opened up and wealth not accumulated are not the ruin of a state. But when those above have no rites and those below have no learning, lawless people rise up, and the state will perish any day.' The Ode says, 'Heaven is now overturning things; do not be so slack and careless.' 'Slack and careless' means 'dawdling'. To serve one's ruler without righteousness, to come and go from office without regard to the rites, and to speak against the Way of the former kings: that is dawdling. Therefore it is said, 'To press one's ruler to do what is difficult is called respectful; to set forth good and shut out evil is called reverent; to say "My ruler is not capable" is called robbing him.'"

Mencius said, "The compass and square are the perfection of the circle and the square. The sage is the perfection of human relations. One who wishes to be a ruler should fulfil the way of a ruler; one who wishes to be a minister should fulfil the way of a minister. In both cases, simply take Yao and Shun as models. Not to serve one's ruler as Shun served Yao is to fail to respect one's ruler. Not to govern the people as Yao governed them is to rob one's people. Confucius said, 'There are two ways only: benevolence and its absence.' A ruler who oppresses his people to the extreme will himself be killed and his state destroyed. One who does so less will put himself in danger and see his state diminished. He will be named 'You' [the Benighted] or 'Li' [the Cruel], and even filial sons and loving grandsons will not be able to change it in a hundred generations. The Ode says, 'The mirror for Yin is not far off; it is in the age of the sovereigns of Xia.' This is what it means."

Mencius said, "The Three Dynasties won the world by benevolence and lost it by the lack of benevolence. So it is too with the decline and rise, the survival and fall of states. If the Son of Heaven is not benevolent, he cannot keep the four seas. If a feudal lord is not benevolent, he cannot keep the altars of his state. If a minister or great officer is not benevolent, he cannot keep his ancestral temple. If a scholar or commoner is not benevolent, he cannot keep his four limbs. To hate death and ruin and yet delight in not being benevolent is like hating drunkenness and yet forcing oneself to drink."

Mencius said, "If you love others and they are not drawn to you, turn back to your own benevolence. If you govern others and they are not well governed, turn back to your own wisdom. If you treat others with courtesy and they do not respond, turn back to your own respect. Whenever your actions do not get the result you seek, turn back and look for the cause in yourself. When your own person is correct, the world will turn to you. The Ode says, 'Always be in harmony with the mandate [of Heaven]; seek for yourself much happiness.'"

Mencius said, "People have a common saying: 'The world, the state, the family.' The root of the world is in the state; the root of the state is in the family; the root of the family is in one's own person."

Mencius said, "Governing is not difficult: do not offend the great houses. What the great houses admire, the whole state admires; what the whole state admires, the whole world admires. So the teaching of virtue spreads abundantly and overflows the four seas."

Mencius said, "When the Way prevails in the world, those of lesser virtue serve those of greater virtue, and those of lesser worth serve those of greater worth. When the Way does not prevail, the small serve the large and the weak serve the strong. Both of these are of Heaven. Those who follow Heaven survive; those who go against Heaven perish. Duke Jing of Qi said, 'Unable to give orders and unwilling to take them: that is to cut oneself off from others.' With tears flowing he gave his daughter in marriage to Wu. Nowadays small states take large states as their teachers, yet are ashamed to take orders from them. That is like a student being ashamed to take orders from his teacher. If they are ashamed of it, nothing is better than to take King Wen as their teacher. Taking King Wen as teacher, a large state would in five years, and a small state in seven, certainly come to govern the world. The Ode says, 'The descendants of Shang numbered more than a hundred thousand; but when God had given the mandate, they submitted to Zhou. They submitted to Zhou, for Heaven's mandate is not constant. The officers of Yin, handsome and quick, pour the libations in our capital.' Confucius said, 'Against benevolence, numbers count for nothing. If the ruler of a state loves benevolence, he will have no rival in the world.' Now to wish to have no rival in the world and yet not use benevolence is like holding something hot without first wetting one's hands. The Ode says, 'Who can hold something hot without first wetting his hands?'"

Mencius said, "Can one talk with those who are not benevolent? They are at ease in their danger and profit from their calamities; they delight in the very things that will destroy them. If one could talk with those who are not benevolent, how would there be any ruined states or fallen houses? There was a boy who sang, 'When the water of the Canglang is clear, I can wash my hat-strings in it; when the water of the Canglang is muddy, I can wash my feet in it.' Confucius said, 'Listen, my young friends! When it is clear, one washes one's hat-strings in it; when it is muddy, one washes one's feet in it. The water brings this on itself.' A man must first insult himself before others will insult him. A family must first destroy itself before others will destroy it. A state must first attack itself before others will attack it. The Tai Jia says, 'When Heaven sends calamities, they can still be escaped; when we bring calamities on ourselves, we cannot survive.' This is what it means."

Mencius said, "Jie and Zhou lost the world because they lost the people; they lost the people because they lost their hearts. There is a way to win the world: win the people, and you will win the world. There is a way to win the people: win their hearts, and you will win the people. There is a way to win their hearts: gather for them what they desire, and do not impose on them what they hate. That is all. The people turn to benevolence as water flows downward and as beasts run to the wilds. So it is the otter that drives the fish into the deep pool, the hawk that drives the birds into the thicket, and Jie and Zhou who drove the people to Tang and Wu. If among the rulers of the world today there were one who loved benevolence, all the other lords would drive the people to him. Even if he did not wish to become king, he could not help it. Those who wish to become king today are like a man who has been ill for seven years seeking moxa that has been dried for three. If he has not laid it up, he will not get it in all his life. If they do not set their minds on benevolence, they will be in sorrow and disgrace all their lives and end in death and ruin. The Ode says, 'How can they be good? They all sink together into the deep.' This is what it means."

Mencius said, "With those who do violence to themselves one cannot talk; with those who throw themselves away one cannot act. To speak against the rites and righteousness is called doing violence to oneself. To say 'I cannot dwell in benevolence or follow righteousness' is called throwing oneself away. Benevolence is man's peaceful home; righteousness is man's straight road. To leave the peaceful home empty and not live in it, to abandon the straight road and not walk on it: how sad!"

Mencius said, "The Way is near, yet people seek it far away. The task is easy, yet people seek it in what is hard. If everyone loved their parents and treated their elders as elders, the world would be at peace."

Mencius said, "If those in low positions do not have the confidence of their superiors, they cannot govern the people. There is a way to gain the confidence of one's superiors: if one is not trusted by one's friends, one will not gain the confidence of one's superiors. There is a way to be trusted by one's friends: if one does not please one's parents in serving them, one will not be trusted by one's friends. There is a way to please one's parents: if one looks within and is not sincere, one will not please one's parents. There is a way to make oneself sincere: if one does not understand what is good, one will not make oneself sincere. Therefore sincerity is the way of Heaven, and to think how to be sincere is the way of man. There has never been one who was perfectly sincere and yet did not move others; and there has never been one who was not sincere and yet could move others."

Mencius said, "Bo Yi fled from Zhou and lived on the shore of the northern sea. When he heard that King Wen had risen, he roused himself and said, 'Why not go and join him? I hear the Lord of the West takes good care of the old.' Taigong fled from Zhou and lived on the shore of the eastern sea. When he heard that King Wen had risen, he roused himself and said, 'Why not go and join him? I hear the Lord of the West takes good care of the old.' These two old men were the greatest elders in the world, and they went over to him: this means the fathers of the world went over to him. When the fathers of the world went over to him, where else would their sons go? If any of the feudal lords practised the government of King Wen, within seven years he would certainly come to govern the world."

Mencius said, "When Qiu was steward to the Ji family, he could do nothing to improve their conduct, and he doubled the grain tax compared with former days. Confucius said, 'Qiu is no disciple of mine. You young men may beat the drum and attack him.' From this we see that those who enrich a ruler who does not practise benevolent government are all rejected by Confucius. How much more those who wage fierce wars for him! When they fight over land, the dead fill the fields; when they fight over cities, the dead fill the cities. This is what is called leading the land to eat human flesh; death is not punishment enough for such a crime. Therefore those who are skilled in war should receive the highest punishment; those who form alliances among the feudal lords should come next; and those who open up wild land and assign the fields [to squeeze the people] should come next."

Mencius said, "Of all the parts of a man, none is better [for revealing him] than the pupils of his eyes. The pupils cannot hide his wickedness. When all is right within his breast, the pupils are bright; when all is not right within his breast, the pupils are dim. Listen to his words and look into his eyes: how can a man hide himself?"

Mencius said, "The respectful do not insult others; the frugal do not rob others. Rulers who insult and rob others, and only fear that others will not submit to them: how can they be respectful or frugal? Can respect and frugality be made out of a pleasant voice and a smiling face?"

Chunyu Kun said, "Is it a rule of propriety that men and women should not touch hands when giving and receiving things?" Mencius said, "It is a rule of propriety." "If one's sister-in-law is drowning, may one pull her out with one's hand?" Mencius said, "One who did not pull out his drowning sister-in-law would be a wolf. That men and women should not touch hands when giving and receiving is the rule of propriety; to pull out a drowning sister-in-law with one's hand is weighing the circumstances." "Now the whole world is drowning. Why do you not pull it out, sir?" Mencius said, "When the world is drowning, one pulls it out with the Way; when a sister-in-law is drowning, one pulls her out with one's hand. Would you have me pull out the world with my hand?"

Gongsun Chou said, "Why is it that a gentleman does not teach his own son?" Mencius said, "Circumstances do not allow it. A teacher must teach what is right. When what is right does not take effect, he follows it with anger. When he follows it with anger, he does harm instead. [The son says,] 'You teach me what is right, but you yourself do not act rightly.' So father and son harm each other, and when father and son harm each other, it is bad. In ancient times men exchanged sons and taught each other's. Between father and son there should be no demanding of goodness. Demanding goodness leads to estrangement, and there is no greater misfortune than estrangement."

Mencius said, "Of all service, which is greatest? Serving one's parents is greatest. Of all keeping, which is greatest? Keeping oneself is greatest. I have heard of those who, without losing themselves, were able to serve their parents; I have never heard of those who lost themselves and were still able to serve their parents. What is not a kind of service? But serving one's parents is the root of all service. What is not a kind of keeping? But keeping oneself is the root of all keeping. When Zengzi looked after Zeng Xi, there was always wine and meat. When the meal was being cleared away, he always asked to whom what was left should be given. If asked whether there was more, he always said, 'There is.' When Zeng Xi died and Zeng Yuan looked after Zengzi, there was always wine and meat. But when the meal was being cleared away, he did not ask to whom what was left should be given; if asked whether there was more, he said, 'There is none left,' meaning to serve it again [at the next meal]. That is what is called looking after the mouth and body. One like Zengzi may be said to have looked after the wishes [of his parent]. To serve one's parents as Zengzi did is what is right."

Mencius said, "It is not enough to find fault with the men in office, nor enough to criticise the government. Only a great man can correct what is wrong in the ruler's heart. If the ruler is benevolent, everyone will be benevolent; if the ruler is righteous, everyone will be righteous; if the ruler is correct, everyone will be correct. Once the ruler is set right, the state will be settled."
Mencius said, "There is praise that one did not expect, and there is blame that comes when one is striving for perfection."
Mencius said, "When people speak lightly, it is because they have not been taken to task."
Mencius said, "The trouble with people is that they are fond of being teachers to others."

Yuezhengzi came to Qi in the train of Ziao. Yuezhengzi went to see Mencius. Mencius said, "So you have come to see me too?" Yuezhengzi said, "Master, why do you say such a thing?" Mencius said, "How many days have you been here?" "Since the day before yesterday." "Since the day before yesterday! Then is it not right that I should say such a thing?" "My lodgings had not been settled." "Have you heard that one should wait until one's lodgings are settled before going to see one's elders?" Yuezhengzi said, "I have done wrong."
Mencius said to Yuezhengzi, "You came here in the train of Ziao only for the eating and drinking. I never thought that you would study the Way of the ancients for the sake of eating and drinking."

Mencius said, "There are three things that are unfilial, and to have no heir is the greatest of them. Shun married without telling [his parents] because he feared he would have no heir. The gentleman considers that it was as if he had told them."

Mencius said, "The substance of benevolence is serving one's parents. The substance of righteousness is obeying one's elder brother. The substance of wisdom is knowing these two and not departing from them. The substance of the rites is regulating and adorning these two. The substance of music is delighting in these two. When there is delight, they grow; once they grow, how can they be stopped? When they cannot be stopped, then without knowing it one's feet begin to dance and one's hands begin to wave."

Mencius said, "The whole world was greatly pleased and about to turn to him, yet he regarded the world being pleased and turning to him as no more than grass. Only Shun was like this. He held that if one could not win one's parents' hearts, one could not be a man, and if one could not be obedient to one's parents, one could not be a son. Shun did everything in the way of serving his parents, until Gusou was brought to be pleased. When Gusou was brought to be pleased, the world was transformed. When Gusou was brought to be pleased, all the fathers and sons in the world found their proper places. This is what is called great filial piety."
